# Report card {#sec-reportcard} This chapter answers the simplest question: **how often is the model right, for each thing it predicts, compared with the sportsbooks?** Every number comes from seasons the model never saw. Each season from 2021 to 2025 is predicted by a model trained only on earlier seasons (`scripts/scorecard.py`, read live from `models/scorecard.json`). ## The scorecard ::: {#tbl-scorecard .cell tbl-cap='Out-of-sample report card, 2021–2025. Market = closing lines (moneylines de-vigged; swapped moneylines removed).' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
Measure Model Sportsbooks
Target
Winner Picks the right winner 70.6% 71.9%
Winner AUC (0.5 coin flip, 1 perfect) 0.772 0.793
Winner Brier score (lower is better) 0.191 0.183
Spread Average miss on the final margin 12.71 pts 12.12 pts
Spread Covers, model's side vs opening line 50.1% —
Spread Covers, model's side vs closing line 49.2% —
Total Average miss on total points 12.91 pts 12.54 pts
Total Wins, model's side vs opening line 51.0% —
Total Wins, model's side vs closing line 50.3% —
Team points Average miss on each team's points 9.13 pts 8.77 pts
``` ::: ::: Reading it: - **Picking winners: good.** The model picks the right winner about 7 times in 10, close to the sportsbooks. An AUC around 0.77 is solid for college football. - **Beating the price: not yet.** Against the spread and the total, betting the model's side lands near 50%, and you need 52.4% at −110 just to break even. Betting the moneyline where the model is more confident than the books returned **−4.5%** (@sec-decisions). - **Accuracy gap:** the books are about 0.4–0.6 points more accurate on margins and totals. ## Halves and quarters ::: {#tbl-periods-card .cell tbl-cap='Halves and quarters: average miss vs guessing the average (no sportsbook lines yet).' execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
model (pts) guess the average (pts) improvement

Q1 4.18 4.47 -6%

Q4 4.39 4.41 -1%
``` ::: ::: ## Where the model falls behind The most useful part of a report card is where the grade is lowest. The gap is how many points worse than the sportsbooks the model's margin is. ::: {#cell-fig-gaps .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Margin error gap vs the closing line, by part of the season and by spread size (points; lower is better).](reportcard_files/figure-html/fig-gaps-output-1.svg){#fig-gaps} ::: ::: Three weak spots stand out: **the first weeks of the season**, **bowls and the playoff**, and **blowouts** (spreads above three touchdowns). In the middle and late regular season the model is almost level with the market. The first weak spot was addressed with preseason information (@sec-improvements); the others are on the roadmap.
